content: The Chess World Cup 2017 was won by Levon Aronian [3].

The United States suspended the convertibility of the U.S. dollar to gold in 1971 [2]. Prior to this, the U.S. government had taken the nation off the gold standard in March and April 1933, causing the dollar's value to sink [3].
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault officially opened on February 26, 2008 [2], although the first seeds arrived in January 2008 [2]. The vault was scheduled to open in late 2008 [3].
The national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago, "Forged from the Love of Liberty," was composed by Patrick S. Castagne in 1962 [1][3].

Bourbon Street is a historic street in the heart of New Orleans' oldest neighborhood, the French Quarter, famous for its many bars and strip clubs [1]. St. Charles Avenue is a thoroughfare in New Orleans, Louisiana, and is famous for the dozens of mansions that adorn the tree-lined boulevard for much of the uptown section [2].

The song "Do You Want to Know a Secret" was sung by George Harrison, and it was primarily composed by John Lennon but credited to Lennon–McCartney [1]. Harrison sang this song because Lennon felt it suited him best, and it was recorded as part of their marathon ten-hour recording session on 11 February 1963 [2].

The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution was ratified by the states on December 6, 1865 [2]. It was proclaimed as adopted by Secretary of State William H. Seward on December 18, 1865 [2].

The song "Don't Matter to Me" by Drake, featuring posthumous vocals from Michael Jackson, was released as the album's fourth single on July 6, 2018 [1]. The song peaked at number two on the "Billboard" Hot 100 chart, making it Jackson's 30th top-ten entry [2].

England won the FIFA World Cup in 1966, when they hosted the finals and defeated West Germany 4–2 in the final [1]. This was England's only FIFA World Cup title, with their best ever performance being their win in the 1966 tournament [2].

Booker T. Washington delivered his famous Atlanta Exposition Speech on September 18, 1895, to a predominantly white audience at the Cotton States and International Exposition in Atlanta, Georgia [3]. The speech laid the foundation for the Atlanta compromise, an agreement between African-American leaders and Southern white leaders, in which Southern blacks would work meekly and submit to white political rule, while Southern whites guaranteed that blacks would receive basic education and due process of law [4].
The state of Louisiana adopted a right-to-work law in 1976 [3].

The first Indigenous Games (or "NAIG") were held in 1990 in Edmonton, Alberta [1]. The dream to hold a Games for the Indigenous Peoples of North America began in the 1970s, with the Native Summer Games held in Enoch, Alberta, Canada in 1971 drawing 3,000 participants [2]. The 2017 North American Indigenous Games were held in Toronto, Ontario, Canada from July 16 to 23, featuring 5,000 athletes aged 13 to 19 in 14 sports [3].

The Dark Tower series by Stephen King consists of eight books [1]. The series incorporates themes from multiple genres, including dark fantasy, science fantasy, horror, and Western, and describes a "gunslinger" and his quest toward a tower, the nature of which is both physical and metaphorical [1].

The Myrtle Beach SkyWheel is located in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, and was the second-tallest extant Ferris wheel in North America when it opened on May 20, 2011 [1]. It is situated near Plyler Park and was the tallest Ferris wheel in the United States east of the Mississippi River at the time of its construction [3].

The third season of the animated television series "Rick and Morty" originally aired on Cartoon Network's late-night programming block, Adult Swim [1]. The season premiered with "The Rickshank Rickdemption" on April 1, 2017, and concluded on October 1, 2017 [1]. The season comprised ten episodes and originally aired Sundays at 11:30 p.m EST. on Adult Swim [2].

The term that refers to linking a currency value to the value of gold is the "gold standard" [1]. Under the gold standard, a country's government declares that it will freely exchange currency for actual gold at the designated exchange rate [2]. This "rule of exchange” allows anyone to enter the central bank and exchange coins or currency for pure gold or vice versa [2].

The Olympic football tournament was first introduced at the 1908 Summer Olympics, which was organized by England's Football Association and featured amateur players only [5]. The first Olympic football competition in which professionals were allowed was the 1984 Summer Olympics, which started on July 29 and ended on August 11 [1][2].

The Cleveland Browns returned to the NFL in 1999, after a three-year period of deactivation [1]. This marked the return of professional football to the city of Cleveland, Ohio for the first time since the 1995 season [3].
The city of St. Petersburg is located in Pinellas County, Florida [1]. It is situated on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa [1].

The first handheld amateur camera was introduced by George Eastman in 1888, with the Kodak camera, which could easily be carried and handheld during its operation [3]. The Cinematograph, developed by brothers Auguste and Louis Lumière in the 1890s, was also compact enough to be mounted on a tripod or carried by the cameraman [1].

In the 2010 adaptation of "Alice Through the Looking Glass," the White Queen is portrayed by Anne Hathaway, who described her interpretation of the character as "a punk-rock vegan pacifist" [2]. In the 1987 animated film "Alice Through the Looking Glass," the White Queen is voiced by Phyllis Diller [4].

The Ordinance of Secession was drafted and ratified in 1860 and 1861 by each of the thirteen southern states, with each state and the Territory of Arizona ratifying its own ordinance of secession [4]. In South Carolina, the Ordinance of Secession was signed on December 20, 1860, with William Henry Gist being one of the signers [2].
The cost of hosting the Rio Olympics was estimated at USD 4.6 billion [1], which compares to the costs of USD 40-44 billion for Beijing 2008 and USD 51 billion for Sochi 2014 [1].
The festival of Holi marks the end of winter and the beginning of spring [2]. It also celebrates the beginning of the new year and is an occasion to reset and renew relationships [3].

The song "Brown Eyes" was composed and sung by Christine McVie, and original guitarist Peter Green also took part in the sessions for the track [1]. The song "Pretty Brown Eyes" was co-written by Cody Simpson with songwriting duo Timothy and Theron Thomas (brothers from Planet VI or Rock City) and Vasquez Castillo [2].
The winner of the final Head of Household (HOH) in Big Brother 20 was not specified in the provided search results [1][2][3][4][5].

The United States purchased the Gadsden Purchase from Mexico, with the first draft of the treaty signed on December 30, 1853, by James Gadsden, U.S. ambassador to Mexico, and by Antonio López de Santa Anna, president of Mexico [1]. The U.S. Senate voted in favor of ratifying the treaty with amendments on April 25, 1854 [1].
The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) was established by Reverend John Flynn on May 15, 1928, in Cloncurry, Queensland [1]. This experiment later became the Royal Flying Doctor Service [2].

The song "Genie in a Bottle" was released on June 22, 1999, by RCA Records as the lead single from Christina Aguilera's self-titled debut album [1]. It reached number one on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and stayed there for five consecutive weeks, becoming the biggest summer song of 1999 [2].

The second season of the Netflix series "Jessica Jones" was released on March 8, 2018, to coincide with International Women's Day [1]. The season was released after the miniseries "The Defenders" in 2017 [2].

The end of Roman rule in Britain occurred when the Romano-Britons expelled the magistrates of the usurper Constantine III around 410, in response to his failures to protect the island [1]. The Romano-Britons had first appealed to Rome for aid, but when no help was forthcoming, they took charge of their own affairs [2].

The torch at the 2012 Olympics was lit by Sir Steve Redgrave, who carried the flame into the stadium and passed it on to one of a team of seven young athletes and one young volunteer, each nominated by a famous British Olympian [1]. The flame was received by Redgrave from young footballer Jade Bailey, who was the torchbearer on the boat piloted by David Beckham [2].

The Latin word "camera obscura" translates to "dark room" [1], describing the natural optical phenomenon where an image of a scene is projected through a small hole, forming an inverted image on a surface opposite the opening [2]. The term "camera obscura" also refers to constructions or devices that utilize this principle within a box, tent, or room [4].

The Boston Red Sox set a franchise record for the most wins in a season with 105 victories in the 1912 season [3]. They also set a new franchise record for wins in a season by surpassing the prior mark of 105 that had been set in 1912, in the 2018 season [2].
The winner of Britain's Got Talent in 2015 was Jules O'Dwyer & Matisse, a dog tricks duo [1].

The East India Company introduced cricket to India [1]. Cricket had been introduced to India by British sailors of the East India Company, with the earliest reference to cricket being played in the Indian sub-continent in 1721 [3]. The Parsi community, who were in close contact with the Imperial British, were among the first to start playing cricket in India [4].
The character of Matt Brody on the original "Baywatch" was portrayed by David Charvet [1].

The Black Stallion, the title character from author Walter Farley's bestselling series, is an Arab stallion [2]. In the series, the stallion's backstory is furnished in later books, and he is known as the Black or Shêtân, with Shaytan being the Arabic word for "devil" [2].
The most plentiful category of rocks in the Earth's crust is igneous rocks, making up about 64.7% of the Earth's crust by volume [1].

The song "Fooled Around and Fell in Love" was written and performed by blues guitarist Elvin Bishop, who did not sing lead vocals on the track, instead inviting vocalist Mickey Thomas to sing it [1]. The song appeared on Bishop's 1975 album "Struttin' My Stuff" and was released as a single the following year, peaking at #3 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 singles chart in May 1976 [1].
The song "As Time Goes By" was written by Herman Hupfeld in 1931 [1][3]. It became most famous in 1942 when part of it was sung by the character Sam in the movie "Casablanca" [1][3].

The systolic blood pressure value is the pressure when the ventricles are contracting, near the end of the cardiac cycle [1]. This pressure is the peak pressure in the arteries, occurring when the ventricles are contracting [1]. A systolic blood pressure of > 70 mmHg can be estimated to be present in patients with a palpable carotid, femoral, and radial pulses [2].
In the context of "That's So Raven," Raven married a Tamaranean man named General Phy'zzon out of love, but he died trying to defend New Tamaran against the Sun Eater [2].

The film "There Will Be Blood" takes place in Southern California during the oil boom of the late 19th and early 20th centuries [2]. The story revolves around a silver miner-turned-oilman's ruthless quest for wealth [2].
The New York Jets lost the first televised Monday Night Football game to the Cleveland Browns with a score of 31–21 [1].

The New England Patriots won three Super Bowls in a row from 2001 to 2004 [1], and also won back-to-back Super Bowls in the 2014 and 2016 seasons [1]. The Patriots became only the second team to win three Super Bowls in four years after winning Super Bowl XXXIX [4].

Network address translation (NAT) is a method of remapping one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a traffic routing device [1][2]. This technique is used to conserve global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion and hides an entire IP address space, usually consisting of private IP addresses, behind a single IP address in another, usually public address space [3].

The third installment in the "How to Train Your Dragon" trilogy, titled "How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World," was originally scheduled for release on June 17, 2016 [3], but the release date was later moved to February 22, 2019 [2].

The song "I'm Not Gonna Miss You" was co-written by Glen Campbell and producer Julian Raymond, and was released on September 30, 2014, for the soundtrack to the documentary "Glen Campbell: I'll Be Me" [1]. The song was nominated for Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards, and was performed by Tim McGraw during the ceremony [2].

The role of Cindy Lou Who was played by actress Taylor Momsen in the 2000 live-action film "How the Grinch Stole Christmas!" [1]. However, in the 1955 film "Good Morning, Miss Dove", the uncredited role of a schoolgirl was played by actress Carol Sydes, who later became known as Cindy Carol [4]. In the 2010 film, the role of Cindy Lou was played by actress Emily Grace Reaves [3].

The ribeye is a beef steak from the rib section of a beef animal, specifically spanning from ribs six through twelve [1]. It is originally the center portion of the rib steak, without the bone, and is considered a more flavorful cut due to the muscle being exercised by the animal during its life [2].

The Lion King premiered on Broadway at the New Amsterdam Theater on October 15, 1997, with the official opening on November 13, 1997 [1]. It later moved to the Minskoff Theatre on June 13, 2006, where it is still running [1].

The Golden State Warriors are an American professional basketball team based in Oakland, California [1]. They relocated to the San Francisco Bay Area in 1962 and undertook the city's name, before changing its geographic moniker to Golden State in 1971 [1]. The franchise adopted its brand name Golden State Warriors prior to the 1971–72 season, in order to suggest that the team represented the entire state of California [3].

The music for the film "How to Train Your Dragon" was composed by John Powell [1]. Powell's score earned him his first Academy Award nomination and his third BAFTA nomination [1]. Powell had previously collaborated with DreamWorks Animation on five films, but "How to Train Your Dragon" was his first solo score for the studio [3].

The first rocket to reach space was a German V-2 rocket, which achieved this feat on October 3, 1942, when it landed 193 km away after following its trajectory perfectly [2]. The first liquid-fueled rocket was launched by Robert Goddard on March 16, 1926, in Auburn, Massachusetts [3].

Hungry Jack's owns and operates or sub-licenses all of the Burger King/Hungry Jack's restaurants in Australia, with over 390 locations across the country [4]. It is the master franchise for the country, responsible for licensing new operators, opening its own stores, and performing standards oversight of franchised locations in Australia [4]. Hungry Jack's is the second largest franchise of Burger King in the world, with over 390 locations across Australia [4].
The song "You Know Better Than I" (also known as "Better Than I") from the 2000 direct-to-video film "Joseph: King of Dreams" is performed by Joseph (David Campbell) [2][3].

The song "If I Were a Boy" was originally recorded by BC Jean, whose record company initially rejected it [1]. The song was later recorded by Beyoncé for her third studio album "I Am... Sasha Fierce" [1].

The 1999 film "10 Things I Hate About You" is a loose modernization of William Shakespeare's comedy "The Taming of the Shrew," retold in a late-1990s American high school setting [3]. Many scenes in the film were shot at Stadium High School in Tacoma, Washington [1].

According to the Laws of the Game (2018/19), a player may only be substituted during a stoppage in play and with the permission of the referee [3]. The player to be substituted must have left the field of play before the substitute may enter the field of play [3].

The highest natural point in Texas is Guadalupe Peak, located in Guadalupe Mountains National Park, with an elevation of above sea level [1]. The highest peak in the county within El Paso is North Franklin Mountain at 7,192 feet [2].

The author of the influential book "An Essay on the Principle of Population" was Thomas Robert Malthus, who anonymously published the book in 1798 [1]. The book predicted a grim future due to the mismatch between population growth and food production, unless births were controlled [1]. Malthus's book, which was revised for over 28 years, fueled debate about the size of the population and its effects on human happiness [1].
Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played at the halftime show during Super Bowl XLIII [3].
The first season of the TV series "Sherlock" consisted of three 90-minute episodes [1]. A total of 13 episodes have been produced, with four three-part series airing from 2010 to 2017 [4].
The movie "Summer of '42" was filmed on Nantucket Island, off the coast of Cape Cod [2]. Scenes at the old sawmill were filmed at Cross Lumber Company in Vaiden, Mississippi [1].
The Portuguese referred to the region that is now known as Mumbai as "Bombaim" [1][2]. The name possibly originated from the Galician-Portuguese phrase "bom baim," meaning "good little bay" [4].
In the TV show "Still Game," the character Winston buys several electric heaters at an outdoor market in Possilpark [1].

The ratio of the wave height to its wavelength is not explicitly stated in the provided documents. However, the significant wave height, which is a measure of the wave height, is defined as the mean wave height of the highest third of the waves [1] or four times the standard deviation of the surface elevation [3].
The New York Knicks last won an NBA championship in 1973 [1][2].
Disneyland Paris encompasses two theme parks: Disneyland Park and Walt Disney Studios Park [3].

Ragtime music started to gain popularity in the 1890s, particularly with the emergence of more sophisticated African-American styles such as the cakewalk and ragtime music [1]. By the start of the 20th century, ragtime had become widely popular throughout North America, with people of various subcultures listening to, dancing to, performing, and writing it [3].

Yuzuru Hanyu became the first male figure skater to win two consecutive gold medals at the 2018 Winter Olympics [1]. Aliona Savchenko and Bruno Massot became Olympic champions in the pairs figure skating competition at the 2018 Winter Olympics [2]. Adam Rippon won a bronze medal in the figure skating team event at the 2018 Winter Olympics, making him the United States' first openly gay athlete to win a medal at any Winter Olympics [3].

The Ukrainian Army unveiled its new uniforms on August 24, 2016, modeled on British military styles and incorporating details from the uniforms worn by the Ukrainian People's Army [1]. The U.S. Army began issuing the Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP) uniforms on October 1, 2018, and all Airmen will be required to own OCP uniforms by April 1, 2021 [2].

The Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series in 1980, defeating the Kansas City Royals in game 6 on October 21, 1980 [1][3]. The team also won the World Series in 2008, with their first major sports championship for Philadelphia since the 1983 NBA Finals [2][5].

The role of Ingrid on the TV series "Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman" was initially played by Ashley Jones, but Jennifer Youngs took over the character in its second appearance [1]. The character of Colleen Cooper was played by Erika Flores initially, but she left the role in 1995, and the role was then recast with Jessica Bowman [2].

The process of creating an RNA molecule using DNA as a template is called transcription [2]. This process is mediated by a DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, which copies the sequence of a DNA strand into RNA [5].

The third season of "RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars" premiered on January 25, 2018 [2]. The season was announced in August 2017, and 9 of the 10 cast members were revealed during a VH1 television special titled "Exclusive Queen Ruveal," which aired on October 20, 2017 [3].

Piper Chapman is a fictional character and the protagonist of the Netflix series "Orange Is the New Black," played by Taylor Schilling [2][3]. She is based on Piper Kerman, author of the non-fiction book "", upon which the series is based [2][3].

The first commercially available cellular phone, the Motorola DynaTAC 8000x, was released in the United States in 1983 [2]. Martin Cooper, a former general manager for the systems division at Motorola, led a team that produced the DynaTAC 8000x, the first commercially available cellular phone small enough to be easily carried, and made the first phone call from it in 1973 [3].
The von Trapp family escaped to Switzerland on foot after driving to the Swiss border [1]. The final scene shows the family hiking on the Obersalzberg near the German town of Berchtesgaden [4].

The murderer in the first series of Broadchurch was revealed to be Joe Miller, DS Ellie Miller's husband [2]. This twist was a result of a "lightbulb moment" experienced by the show's creator and writer, Chris Chibnall, who realized that Joe should be the killer [2].

The film "Ghostbusters" (2016) features a cast that includes Melissa McCarthy, Kristen Wiig, Kate McKinnon, and Leslie Jones [3]. In the movie, the Ghostbusters interact with Mayor Bradley and his secretary Jennifer Lynch [1].

The song "Wall to Wall" was recorded by American singer Chris Brown for his second studio album, "Exclusive" (2007) [1]. Chris Brown's song "Wall to Wall" was inspired by Michael Jackson's "Thriller" and the 1998 film "Blade" [3]. 

However, the song "Talkin' to the Wall" was originally recorded by country singer Warner MacPherson (better known by his stage name Warner Mack) in 1966, which became a top ten hit for him when the song peaked at No. 3 in the Country Singles chart [4].
Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup twice, in 1978 and 1986 [1]. The team also reached the World Cup final in 2014, where it lost to Germany [4].

The first person to successfully land the 900 on film at a competition was BMX-Rider Mat Hoffman in Canada in 1989 [1]. However, Tony Hawk landed "The 900" at the 1999 X-Games after ten failed attempts [2]. In 2010, Bob Burnquist became the first skateboarder to land a "fakie 900" (900-degree reverse-natural rotation), making him the fifth person in history to successfully complete the 900 trick [3].

The McMartin preschool trial is considered the longest and most expensive criminal case in the history of the United States legal system, lasting seven years and costing $15 million [1]. The trial "United States v. Anthony Accetturo et al." was notable for being the longest federal trial in history, lasting 21 months [3].
In the episode "He Could Be The One," Miley Stewart, also known as Hannah Montana, chooses Jake over Jesse [2].

The first recipients of the Bharat Ratna were politician C. Rajagopalachari, philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and scientist C. V. Raman, who were honoured in 1954 [1]. Former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri became the first individual to be honoured posthumously [1].
The movie "It" (2017) is set in the summer of 1989 in Derry, Maine [2]. The film's principal photography began in the Riverdale neighborhood of Toronto on June 27, 2016 [1].
The twins who played on the sitcom "Everybody Loves Raymond" were Sawyer and Sullivan Sweeten, who were cast on the show when they were six months old [2].
The song "Next to Me" is recorded by American rock band Imagine Dragons, with the lead singer being Dan Reynolds [1][2][3].

One prominent pioneer in the field of eyewitness research was Hugo Münsterberg, whose book "On the Witness Stand" (1908) demonstrated the fallibility of eyewitness accounts [1]. Gary L. Wells has further developed methods to evaluate eyewitness identification evidence and has written about the strengths and weaknesses of alternative research methods for eyewitness testimony [2]. Judith Daylen has also contributed to assessing the reliability of eyewitness testimony, including a 1986 study with John C. Yuille that concluded eyewitness testimony is often reliable and has merit [3].

The Shema is found in the Torah in Deuteronomy 6:4, which states "Hear, O Israel: the our God, the is one" [1]. The recitation of the Shema in the liturgy consists of three portions: Deuteronomy 6:4-9, 11:13-21, and Numbers 15:37-41 [2].

Michael Jordan's last season as a Bull was the 1997-1998 season [1], during which the Chicago Bulls won their sixth championship in eight years [2]. Jordan retired for the second time on January 13, 1999 [2].

The first Krispy Kreme store in North Carolina was located in a rented building on South Main Street in Winston-Salem in what is now called historic Old Salem [1]. The first Krispy Kreme bakery outside the South opened in Akron, Ohio, in 1939 [1].

The Tin Woodman states that he has neither heart nor brain, but cares nothing for the loss of his brain [1]. Buddy Ebsen, the original actor to play the Tin Man, is heard on the group vocals of "We're Off To See The Wizard" in the soundtrack of the 1939 film "The Wizard of Oz" [2].

The Vietnam Veterans Memorial was dedicated on Veterans Day, 1982, on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. [1]. The construction of the memorial began on March 16, 1982, with the official ground-breaking on March 26, 1982, and was finished in late October 1982 [2].
The film "Places in the Heart" was filmed in Waxahachie, Texas [1].
A standard match in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege lasts four minutes for casual play and three minutes for competitive play [2].
The 2016 Kilkenny Senior Hurling Championship was won by O'Loughlin Gaels after a 0-19 to 1-12 defeat of Ballyhale Shamrocks in the final [1].

The instrument that you blow into with a keyboard is the melodica, also known as the pianica, blow-organ, key harmonica, free-reed clarinet, face piano or melodyhorn [4]. This instrument has a musical keyboard on top and is played by blowing air through a mouthpiece that fits into a hole in the side of the instrument.
After the death of Qutub ud din Aibak, his successor was Shams ud-Din Iltutmish [1].

The National Basketball Association (NBA) had eight franchises in the 1953-54 season: the New York Knicks, Boston Celtics, Philadelphia Warriors, Minneapolis Lakers, Rochester Royals, Fort Wayne Pistons, Tri-Cities Blackhawks, and Syracuse Nationals [3].
The character of the older Dottie Hinson in the 1992 film "A League of Their Own" was played by Lynn Cartwright [1].

Neil Armstrong received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Nixon [1]. He was also awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Richard Nixon, along with his Apollo 11 crewmates [3].
The song "(Remember Me) I'm the One Who Loves You" was written and originally sung by Stuart Hamblen in 1950 [1]. The song was also a hit for Ernest Tubb the same year, and Dean Martin in 1965 [2].

The only child of a president to be born in the White House was Esther Cleveland, who was born on September 9, 1893, as the second child of Grover Cleveland, 22nd and 24th President of the United States [1].

To change a lead atom into a gold atom, nuclear experiments have successfully transmuted lead into gold, but the process is expensive and not feasible for routine manufacture [1]. In 1980, Glenn Seaborg transmuted several thousand atoms of bismuth into gold at the Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory using nuclear physics and removing protons and neutrons from the bismuth atoms [3].

Michael Moriarty, the actor who portrayed Ben Stone in the TV drama "Law & Order", left the show in 1994 [3]. His departure from the series stemmed from his dispute with the network and U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno, who began promoting legislation to limit portrayals of violence on television in 1993 [2].

The combined waters of Lake Michigan and Lake Huron are joined through the Straits of Mackinac, which is a wide and deep passage [1]. This connection allows for the free exchange of water between the two lakes, making them hydrologically a single lake [1].

The Roman emperor Constantine established Sunday as a day of rest in AD 321 [3][4]. This change became more universally accepted with the establishment of Constantine's Sunday law of 321 AD and the decree at the Council of Laodicea that in canon 29 declared that Christians should avoid work on Sunday [2][5].

The song "Fairytale of New York" was written by Jem Finer and Shane MacGowan [1]. The song's inspiration included Sergio Leone's film "Once Upon a Time in America," which influenced the lyrics and introduction, written by MacGowan [2]. The song was originally written in 1985 by Finer, but MacGowan later came up with a better storyline and improved the lyrics [3].
Dr. Owen Hunt, a character from the medical drama television series "Grey's Anatomy", was portrayed by actor Kevin McKidd [1][2][5].

The main character in the Garage Sale Mystery series is Jennifer Shannon, played by Lori Loughlin [1]. The series also features a cast of characters, including the daughters of the main characters, such as Julie, played by an actress who departed from the cast after the fourth season [3].

The second season of "The Seven Deadly Sins" anime series aired from January 13, 2018 to June 30, 2018 [2]. The series has a total of 24 episodes in its first season, which was released on November 1, 2015 [1].

The character of Admiral on Star Trek: Discovery was played by Vaughn Armstrong, who had previously appeared in various Trek productions [1]. In the same series, the character of Admiral Valdore was played by Brian Thompson [2].
The 2018 FIFA World Cup took place in Russia from June 14 to July 15, 2018 [1]. The 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup was held between June 7 and July 7, 2019 [2][3].

The American crime drama television series "Lie to Me" originally ran on the Fox network from January 21, 2009 to January 31, 2011 [3][4]. The show was canceled by Fox after three seasons, with the official cancellation announced on May 10, 2011 [2].

The song "What a Beautiful Name" is by Australian praise and worship group Hillsong Worship, written and led by Brooke Ligertwood and co-written with Ben Fielding [1]. It won two Dove Awards for Song of the Year and Worship Song of the Year in 2017, and also won the 2018 Grammy Award for Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song [1].

The water in the Blue Lagoon in Iceland comes from the nearby geothermal power plant Svartsengi and is renewed every two days [2]. The rich mineral content in the water is provided by the underground geological layers and pushed up to the surface by the hot water used by the plant [3]. The silicate minerals are the primary cause of the water's milky blue shade [3].

The last mainland population of woolly mammoths existed in the Kyttyk Peninsula of Siberia 9,650 years ago [2]. A small population of woolly mammoths survived on St. Paul Island, Alaska, well into the Holocene with the most recently published date of extinction being 5,600 years B.P [2].

The process that releases nitrogen gas into the atmosphere is denitrification, which is an anaerobic process in which microorganisms reduce nitrate (NO) to atmospheric nitrogen gas (N) [1]. This process is also a reverse of nitrification, where nitrate is reduced to nitrite, then NO, and finally nitrogen [2].
The Vikram Samvat calendar is the official calendar of Nepal [1]. In addition to Nepal, the Vikram Samvat calendar is also recognized in North and East India, and in Gujarat among Hindus [3].
The last person hanged in England was John Robson Walby, who was executed on August 13, 1964, at HM Prison Manchester [2].

The song "Anything You Can Do (I Can Do Better)" was composed by Irving Berlin for the 1946 Broadway musical "Annie Get Your Gun" [1]. The song is a duet, with one male singer and one female singer attempting to outdo each other in increasingly complex tasks [1].

The Ottoman Empire became the new rulers of the Levant after defeating the Mamluk sultanate forces at the Battle of Marj Dabiq on August 24, 1516, and subsequently conquered the region of Palestine by December of the same year [2].
The clear and present danger test was replaced in 1969 with the "imminent lawless action" test, as established in the case of "Brandenburg v. Ohio" [2].
In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Nebula, Gamora's adopted sister, is portrayed by Karen Gillan [4].

The surviving literature written in Old English in Anglo-Saxon England includes genres such as epic poetry, hagiography, sermons, Bible translations, legal works, chronicles, and riddles [1]. The "Anglo-Saxon Chronicle" is a collection of annals in Old English that chronicle the history of the Anglo-Saxons from the 9th century [3]. "Cædmon's Hymn", composed in the 7th century, is often considered the oldest extant poem in English [5].

The character of Charlie on the TV show "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia" is portrayed by Charlie Day [1]. Charlie Kelly is a fictional character on the FX series, co-owner at Paddy's, and a childhood friend of Mac and Dennis [1].

The gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) is the maximum operating weight/mass of a vehicle as specified by the manufacturer, including the vehicle's chassis, body, engine, engine fluids, fuel, accessories, driver, passengers, and cargo, but excluding that of any trailers [1].
